breastfeeding behavior is strongly influenced by breastfeeding intention and that intention to breast feed is influenced by attitude, perceived social support, and self efficacy.
the attitude, self-efficacy and social support are predictors of breastfeeding intention and breastfeeding intention affects breastfeeding behavior.
the maternal attitude, social supports and self efficacy have significant effect on the breast feeding intention and behavior.

the factors that affect the breastfeeding practice in mothers of infants under 1 years of age.
the role of attitude, self efficacy and social support in breastfeeding intention and behavior.
the factors affecting breastfeeding practice among a sample population of Iranian women.

maternal attitude, social supports, and self efficacy were associated with breast feeding intention and behavior among Iranian mothers.
breastfeeding is an important issue that requires the attention of policy makers.
the attitude, perceived social support, self efficacy and breast feeding intention have a positive and significant relationship with each other and with breast feeding behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the breastfeeding intention is a strong predictor of breastfeeding behavior.
breastfeeding intention and behavior are affected by maternal attitude, social and perceived self efficacy.

breastfeeding intention is the main factor influencing breastfeeding behavior.
the attitude, self efficacy and perceived social support are the strongest predictors of intention to breastfeed.
